title: fix(plugin-dashboard): render the declared sub-caption on a dataset-bound KPI tile (objectui#7293)
body:
Fixes #7293

## What was broken

`options.description` is a dashboard metric tile's **sub-caption** slot, and it was
declared end to end while being consumed by nothing:

| layer | state before |
| --- | --- |
| spec slot | accepted (`DashboardWidgetOptionsSchema` rides `.passthrough()`) |
| translation key | declared — `{ns}.dashboards.{dash}.widgets.{id}.subCaption` (objectui#4032 item 4, objectstack#8056) |
| server overlay | live — `translateDashboard` writes the resolved translation onto `options.description` |
| renderer resolver | live — `DashboardRenderer.tWidgetSubCaption` |
| **renderer consumer** | **none on the path a widget actually renders through** |

`tWidgetSubCaption`'s resolved value is attached only to the two **inline** arms of
`getComponentSchema()`. `dataset` is REQUIRED on `DashboardWidgetSchema`, so every
spec-legal widget routes to `DatasetWidget` instead — and that component read the
key nowhere. Four layers of live plumbing pointing at a dead end: the ADR-0049
declared-but-unenforced shape, same family as the `colorVariant` fix (objectui#3359)
sitting a few lines above in the same branch.

Negative baseline, re-derived on this branch point (objectui origin/main@64c3cdd44):

```
$ grep -c description packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DatasetWidget.tsx   ->  0
$ grep -c options     packages/plugin-dashboard/src/DatasetWidget.tsx   -> 25   (positive control)
```

The 0 is a real absence, not a misread file. After this change the same two probes
read 2 and 27.

## The precondition the card rests on, re-read

The card's amplifying argument is "`dataset` is required, so **every** widget the
spec admits takes this path". Triage could verify only the inheritance chain — the
spec package was not installed in that tree. Re-read here against the **published
release**, not any branch:

```
resolved: node_modules/.pnpm/@objectstack+spec@17.4.0_.../@objectstack/spec
DashboardWidgetSchema required keys : id, dataset, values
DashboardWidgetSchema optional keys : 19  (instrument control - isOptional() can answer true)
parse of a valid widget minus dataset -> fails, issue path ["dataset"], code invalid_type
parse of the same doc with dataset    -> succeeds  (behavioural control)
```

Required. The card's "every widget" holds and the p2 rating stands.

## The fix

`DatasetWidget`'s metric branch reads the key and renders it in the caption row,
matching the chrome-less vocabulary that branch already uses (the same one
`MetricWidget`'s `bare` layout uses — no card chrome, no icon chip).

Two decisions worth review:

**Read here, not passed down as a prop.** The card describes the resolved value as
"not passed down", which reads as a prop. It is deliberately not one: **both**
dashboard surfaces route a dataset-bound widget to this single component
(`DashboardRenderer` and `DashboardGridLayout`, objectui#4614). A prop threaded from
one dispatch site would have fixed one surface and left the other silently
unchanged. Reading the key in the one component both surfaces share fixes both.

**Resolved through `pickLocalized`, not a `typeof === 'string'` test.** An authored
inline per-locale map is the vocabulary this field admits — `tWidgetSubCaption`
collapses it with the same seam (objectui#4208). A string-only guard here would
silently drop the map spelling, i.e. re-create this card's own bug class inside its
fix, and objectui#4032 is what a private narrower resolver already cost this
vocabulary. A miss answers the empty string, which collapses to `undefined` and
renders **no node at all**.

## Verification

**Acceptance is a class predicate** — *a dataset-bound metric tile whose author wrote
`options.description` renders that sub-caption* — not "`description` appears
somewhere". New file `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DatasetWidget.subCaption.test.tsx`,
12 cases split into two halves that pin opposite directions:

- **6 control cases, green BEFORE and after.** The no-sub-caption markup is asserted
  byte-for-byte (the same byte string `DatasetWidget.colorVariant.test.tsx` pins
  independently for the same widget), plus five ways of declaring nothing — no
  options bag, a bag without the key, an empty string, a null, a locale map with no
  usable entry. They prove the caption row gained no empty node and no stray
  spacing. **A control that reddens when the subject breaks is not a control**, so
  these must stay green under ablation.
- **6 subject cases, RED before and green after** — plain string, the value the
  server overlaid, an inline per-locale map under `zh` and under `en`, the
  fall-through limb, and the card's own duly#109 repro verbatim.

**Ablation, from the committed tree** (`cf8c7778e`), mutation proven on disk before
the run and restore verified by state:

```
HEAD blob            29b519840fd025c9c5b6d0f4761f149f5f70ef24
working-tree blob    29b519840fd025c9c5b6d0f4761f149f5f70ef24   (at HEAD before mutating)
marker count before  1        inject count before  0
marker count after   0        inject count after   1
mutated blob         c1731ee80bffc647d328dda55fcd5f008f1487ee   (differs -> the edit reached disk)
ABLATED RUN          Tests  6 failed | 41 passed (47)
restored blob        29b519840fd025c9c5b6d0f4761f149f5f70ef24   (back to the HEAD blob)
git diff HEAD        empty
```

The 6 failures are named individually and are **exactly the 6 subject cases**; the
6 control cases and all of `DatasetWidget.colorVariant.test.tsx` stayed green. No
build is involved: the root `vitest.config.mts` aliases every `@object-ui/*`
specifier to that package's `src/`, and the test imports `../DatasetWidget`
relatively, so both legs read source directly.

**Enumerated on two axes.**

*Content axis* — who reads the thing the change says. `packages/sdui-parser`'s
`unconsumed-widget-option` census extracts the consumed-key set from
`DatasetWidget.tsx` **source text** and asserted it equals the spec's declared five.
It went red on this change exactly as designed, naming `description` as the new
member. Updated in the same commit, and made stronger rather than merely wider:
leg 2 now expects the declared set plus the sub-caption key; a **new** case asserts
every accepted key has a read site in the measured file (the fact this PR delivers —
the accepted set no longer outruns the measured read set); and the module header's
bounded `format` / `thresholds` closure claim, which used to ride implicitly on an
equality whose right-hand side can grow, is asserted in its **own** right. The
diagnostic itself is byte-identical: `CONSUMED_WIDGET_OPTION_KEYS` is unchanged.

Note for the reviewer: that census counts **comments** as reads (a documented,
deliberately safe-direction bias), so it stayed green during the ablation — it
guards the census's honesty, not this behaviour. The behavioural guard is the new
test file.

*Position axis* — **who points at this file by `file:line`, and which of those
addresses my insertion moved.** This branch inserts 36 lines into
`DatasetWidget.tsx` (+6 after old line 494, +27 after 837, +3 after 857;
1536 → 1572), so every cross-file citation past old line 494 shifts.

Measured with the tree-wide census objectui#8875 landed while this branch was
open (`scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` — report-only, five
syntaxes, including the bare continuation address that a basename-anchored
probe cannot see; my own single-syntax grep missed exactly that one). Run twice:
once at the branch point, once here. **Positive control: 1267 citations
tree-wide.** Seven target `DatasetWidget.tsx`; five change verdict between the
two runs; the whole blast radius is this one file — nothing cites the two
`sdui-parser` files this PR also edits.

Only **two** were pointing at what they describe *before* this branch existed,
and only those two are repaired here:

| citing site | cites | anchor | verdict before → on branch → after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chart-series-keys-7546.test.ts:146` | `DatasetWidget.tsx:1450` → `:1486` | `const primary = presentedSeries.find((s) =` … `s.dataKey === m);` | resolves → drifted → **resolves** |
| `data-display.ts:1506` | `DatasetWidget.tsx:1450` → `:1486` | same line, byte-identical at 1450 then and 1486 now | resolves → drifted → **resolves** |

The other five were **already false at the branch point**, so they belong to
objectui#8875 and are deliberately untouched — re-addressing a wrong address by
a hunk delta just moves it to a different wrong address:

| citing site | cites | what it claims is there | where that anchor really is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DashboardGridLayout.tsx:51` | `:655` | `dataSource: unknown` | 408 (before every insertion point — never moved) |
| `queryDataset.test.ts:609` | `:590-593` | `drillDims` / `canDrill` | 786 / 789 |
| `datasetPath.test.tsx:47` | `:766-771` | sets the error state | 559 |
| `datasetPath.test.tsx:48` | `:929-934` | renders the error alert | 719-721 |
| `chart-series-keys-7546.test.ts:48` | `:1444-1447` | the `variant` write | 1451-1458 (the cited range is the comment above it) |

⚠️ One of those deserves naming for objectui#8875 rather than fixing here: this
branch's shift flips `datasetPath.test.tsx:48` from `drifted` to `resolves` **by
coincidence**. It is not repaired — it is an unearned green on a citation that
was already wrong, and the census's tree-wide `falseToday` drops by one for a
reason nobody should credit to this PR.

`packages/data-objectstack/CHANGELOG.md:682` also cites this file and is
untouched on two independent grounds: a released changelog is a dated record of
what was true at that release, and its address is before the first insertion
point anyway.

*What the change itself moved.* 5 files changed, plus 2 new (the test and the
changeset). `DatasetWidget.tsx` +38: one import line, one hook, one resolved
constant, one conditionally-rendered span, and the comment block explaining why
the key is read here. The two citation repairs are comment-only, in
`packages/types`, and touch no executable code.

**Runs** (all from the repo root; `pnpm exec vitest run PATHS`, never from a package
directory and never behind a bare `--`):

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| `vitest run packages/plugin-dashboard/ packages/sdui-parser/` | **114 files / 1084 tests passed** |
| `type-check` (both packages) | pass — after building the 13-package dependency closure |
| `lint` (both packages) | 0 errors, 450 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings |
| `check:control-bytes` | OK, 7076 tracked text files |
| `check:phantom-deps` / `check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `check:vi-mock-inherit` | OK |
| `check:i18n-keys` / `check:unreferenced-sources` | OK |
| `scripts/__tests__/unconsumed-widget-option-claim-6186.test.ts` | 6/6 pass |
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | OK — 3 published source files, 1 changeset |

The first `type-check` attempt exited **2** against an unbuilt workspace
(`Cannot find module '@object-ui/core'` in files unrelated to this diff) — a
PREREQUISITE-NOT-MET result, read as NOT MEASURED, and re-run green after the
closure build. `check:readme-exports` self-reports **"the population COLLAPSED —
this run proves nothing"** (24 of 40 packages unbuilt): also NOT MEASURED here, and
measured properly by CI, which builds everything. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` farm is
CI's run, not this seat's.

## 验收备注

Related facts found while doing this, deliberately **not** in this PR:

- **Suggestion 2 on the card — rendering measures after `values[0]` as secondary
  tile values — is not here.** `values[1..]` has no rendering semantics today and
  would gain them, which widens the authoring surface. It is a separate card on the
  manual-floor route. The repro test asserts those measures are still dropped,
  purely as evidence this PR did not ride it in; the successor card is *expected* to
  change that expectation.
- **The card's third path — retiring `options.description` under ADR-0049 — is not
  taken.** Neither triage nor the PM ruled on it; retirement is four layers of
  plumbing plus a spec-side action, another lane entirely.
- **A residual gap, one layer down, needs a successor card.** `tWidgetSubCaption`
  has two limbs: collapse the authored value, then let an i18n **bundle** entry at
  `{ns}.dashboards.{dash}.widgets.{id}.subCaption` win over it. This PR connects the
  first limb (and with it the server-overlay channel, which is how a *served*
  dashboard gets its translation). The bundle limb still cannot reach a
  dataset-bound tile: it needs the dashboard name, which `DatasetWidget` is not
  given by either dispatch site. So on a dashboard loaded from an **app bundle**
  rather than served by the platform, a bundle-only sub-caption — a form
  `tWidgetSubCaption`'s own docblock calls legitimate — still renders nothing. Named
  successor: none yet; **the dedup search for it could not be completed this shift**
  (see the report), so it is handed to the PM to file rather than filed blind.
